- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., +5%+ from prior 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3), model overconfidently holds high forecasts; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- If recent 3–5 day price decline is steep, model fails to reflect mean reversion; forecast should trend upward slightly to counteract overcorrection.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is stable, model often drifts upward; apply slight downward pressure (0.5–1.5%) to avoid false momentum.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
